rules.statement: Executors are not liable to pay interest on a legacy until there is a demand, and lack of funds may be pleaded as an excuse for mora in which case the estate will not be liable to pay interest.
rules.supporting_quote: The principles that appear to be deducible from the various authorities on Roman-Dutch law examined by me and relevant to the present case are- (a) Where the obligation to pay a legacy is suspended until an uncertain date or an uncertain condition (e.g., marriage of the legatee), the executors cannot be put in mora except by demand. (b) That such demand, if extra-judicial should be more or less of a formal nature. (c) That interest runs only from date of mora. (d) That in certain circumstances lack of funds may be pleaded as an excuse by the executors for their mora in which case the estate will not be liable to pay interest.
